dedupe_keys.name: when fire codes meet urban conflagration building damage inspection cohorts for california s chapter 7a standard

description: This analysis package holds individual building damage inspection records, analysis cohorts, model scripts and figure pipelines for a natural-experiment study of California's Chapter 7A wildfire building standard, effective in 2008. It was published on Zenodo (version 1.1, 17 September 2026) by Yang Chen, Yuyi Du, Xin Qi, Hui Zhang and Hanxiong Che of the Three Gorges Laboratory and Chongqing Institute of Green and Intelligent Technology, for a manuscript under review at Science Advances. It covers the Camp (2018), Glass (2020), Woolsey (2018), Eaton (2025) and Palisades (2025) fires, the rebuilding cohort of the 2021 Marshall Fire in Colorado, and a cross-check of the 2023 Lahaina fire, using CAL FIRE damage inspection records; outputs include odds ratios by construction era, density-stratified and value-adjusted models and material transitions. Coverage: five California fires plus Marshall and Lahaina. Access: one 8 MB package on Zenodo with a README. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the companion paper was not yet peer-reviewed when read. Simulation uses: estimating the effect of structure hardening codes on building survival in urban conflagrations. Related records: the Palisades Fire structure-loss dataset and the Moore tornado building-code case study.
